The Korean Railway Workers' Union said the action will begin at 9 a.m. Thursday and last through Dec. 4, with rail workers strictly adhering to safety and other regulations, such as not driving trains faster to make up for lost time, refusing to work overtime and responding to passenger complaints in line with manuals. The union has demanded improvements to the employee promotion system, extra allowances and additional personnel, threatening to launch an indefinite general strike Dec. 10 if the needs are not addressed. It has said rail workers have operated train services on time through endless overtime and holiday work, as well as by working solo in dangerous environments, and that if working to rule leads to delays or suspensions, the effort will prove the lack of personnel. Supporters say Kang is an apolitical pick with experience in leading a government organization and is suitable for a time of strained ties with Washington. Critics, however, cite her lack of intelligence experience and her alleged closeness to China. If confirmed by the National Assembly, Kang, 69, would lead the National Intelligence Service (NIS), an agency central to national security, at a time when Seoul’s ties with Washington are strained over several issues, including Coupang and intelligence sharing. The U.S. has been limiting intelligence sharing with Seoul, a move that is believed to stem from Washington’s suspicion that Unification Minister Chung Dong-young publicly disclosed intelligence on North Korea that Washington had shared with Seoul. items.title: Who is Kang Kum-sil?
items.title_zh: 康琴实是谁？
items.summary: President Lee Jae Myung's pick for spy agency chief, former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil, is drawing attention as she is returning to the main venue of politics after a decade out of the political spotlight. If the National Assembly confirms her for the post, Kang would become the first woman to lead the National Intelligence Service since the agency's predecessor was founded in 1961. Kang, 69, became the first justice minister under President Roh Moo-hyun in 2003. At 46, she was the youngest person and the first woman to hold the post. She remained the only woman to serve as justice minister until Choo Mi-ae, now governor of Gyeonggi Province, was appointed in 2020. Born on Jeju Island in 1957, Kang attended Kyunggi Girls’ High School and studied law at Seoul National University, long seen as the classic path into Korea's legal elite. She passed the bar exam in 1981 and served as a judge from 1983 to 1995. items.title: AI could shorten CSAT's lifespan: Seoul education chief

items.summary: Will artificial intelligence (AI) help hasten the end of Korea’s college entrance exam, with its heavy reliance on multiple-choice questions? Seoul education superintendent Jung Geun-sik sees that possibility, but teachers experimenting with the technology offer a more cautious picture of what it takes to change how students are taught and tested. Speaking at Tuesday’s forum on the future of assessment, Jung recalled his earlier proposal to abolish the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) by 2040. Recent AI developments and high-profile cheating incidents, he said, had led him to question whether the CSAT could even last that long. “At this pace, I wonder whether the CSAT will be viable next year or the year after. I had proposed abolishing it in 14 or 15 years, but the incidents surrounding this year’s exam have left me feeling that its lifespan may be much shorter,” he said. items.title: First lady Kim watches performance by orchestra of visually impaired musicians
items.title_zh: 金正恩夫人观看视障音乐家管弦乐队的表演
items.summary: First lady Kim Hea Kyung on Wednesday attended a concert by an orchestra composed of visually impaired musicians, along with this year's college entrance exam takers. The concert, held in Incheon, west of Seoul, featured the Hyegwang Blind Orchestra, a group of around 50 visually impaired musicians, and was intended to encourage high school seniors who took the grueling college entrance exam earlier this month. The first lady attended the concert at the invitation of a student from Hyegwang School, an educational institution for visually impaired students in Incheon, whom she met last month at an event marking the 100th anniversary of the Korean braille system. Kim praised the orchestra's "enthusiasm and efforts" in creating harmony, while commending the high school seniors in attendance and expressing her hope that they would go on to make their mark in the wider world.

The top court scheduled her sentencing for next Thursday after Kim and a special counsel team both appealed an appellate ruling that sentenced her to a five-year prison term on bribery-related charges, according to the sources. Special counsel Min Joong-ki's team earlier indicted Kim, the wife of former President Yoon Suk Yeol, on charges of receiving expensive gifts from multiple people in return for job appointments and business favors. The alleged gifts include jewelry worth over 100 million won ($74,400) from a construction company chairman in exchange for a government job for his son-in-law in 2022. A district court sentenced Kim to seven years in prison in June after finding her guilty on all counts but the appellate court reduced her sentence in September, acquitting her of some of the charges. The president made the remarks in a post on his X account to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, adding that it was the state's duty to create a society where women can live without fear. In Korea, perpetrators of domestic violence can avoid punishment if victims express a wish not to have them punished. However, the law has come under criticism over concerns that perpetrators may pressure victims into withholding consent to punishment, and that the lack of punishment could lead to more serious violence in the future. Citing a recent series of crimes involving domestic violence, stalking and dating abuse, Lee said the government had failed to "safeguard precious lives despite warning signs and calls for help." They stressed the importance of ensuring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab Strait. Rubio and Prince Faisal discussed efforts to establish security and peace in Sudan, Lebanon, and the wider region, and affirmed their commitment to continued joint action to support stability. Prince Faisal bin Farhan received two separate phone calls from Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation, and Egyptian Expatriates Dr. Badr Abdelatty and Bahraini Minister of Foreign Affairs Dr. Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani. During the calls, the ministers discussed regional developments and condemned the terrorist Houthi militia's continued attacks on civilians and civilian objects in Saudi Arabia and Yemen. items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Tourism has made five digital services available through the unified national application "Tawakkalna," in a move aimed at strengthening digital integration and facilitating beneficiaries' access to tourism sector services. It’s objective is to improve their experience and enhancing service delivery efficiency in line with the development taking place in the Kingdom's tourism sector.The move is part of the ministry's efforts to align its digital services with the Digital Government Authority's directions and strengthen integration with national platforms, expanding access channels for tourism sector services and facilitating their use. The services made available through the Tawakkalna app include applying for a tour guide license; the Ministry of Tourism's licenses and applications; tour guiding training; viewing training applications and certificates issued by the ministry; and checking the list of individuals and entities licensed by the Ministry of Tourism.The services available through Tawakkalna are integrated with the Tourism Platform, launched by the ministry as part of its efforts to develop an integrated digital system for tourism sector services. Beneficiaries can submit their applications through the app, which are then processed through the ministry's digital systems, strengthening service connectivity and ensuring continuity of procedures across various digital channels.The ministry said these services' availability through Tawakkalna represents a further step in its efforts to develop its digital services and provide beneficiaries with wider access options, as part of its fruitful partnerships with other government entities. It added that the launch was the result of ongoing cooperation between the Ministry of Tourism and the Digital Government Authority, affirming that cooperation would continue to provide advanced digital services that help develop the Kingdom's tourism sector.Making these services available through Tawakkalna builds on the Ministry of Tourism's efforts to develop its digital tourism services system, expand access channels, and strengthen integration among its platforms and digital services, providing beneficiaries with an easier and more efficient experience and supporting the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030.

items.title: Minister Al-Saif : Budget sustains growth, enhances investment competitiveness
items.title_zh: Al-Saif部长：预算将支撑经济增长，提升投资竞争力
items.summary: RIYADH —Minister of Investment Fahad Al-Saif said the state budget for fiscal year 2027 reflects the leadership’s commitment to advancing the development goals of Saudi Vision 2030. It also supports efforts to diversify the national economy’s production base and increase the private sector’s contribution.Al-Saif highlighted the Saudi economy’s ability to maintain stability and sustain growth amid global economic and geopolitical changes, reflecting the strength of its foundations. He added that this resilience reinforces investors’ confidence in their ability to maintain and expand their businesses in Saudi Arabia. “The clarity of spending priorities helps the private sector plan its investments and expand its businesses," the minister said. “At the investment ecosystem, we are working with our partners to create opportunities for local and international investors and turn them into productive projects that contribute to transferring knowledge and technology, developing local content and value chains, and creating jobs across various regions of the Kingdom."Al-Saif pointed to indicators of Saudi Arabia’s expanding investment base. Foreign direct investment inflows reached around SR159 billion in 2025, up 33.5%, while gross fixed capital formation totaled around SR1.4 trillion, equivalent to 28.4% of gross domestic product (GDP).He affirmed that the investment ecosystem is working to strengthen the investment environment through economic, legislative, and regulatory reforms and improved services for investors. It also seeks to enable the private sector to expand its high-value investments, thereby enhancing Saudi Arabia’s competitiveness and supporting sustainable economic growth.

items.title: Coalition: Houthi terrorists used drone to attack KAFD tower
items.title_zh: 联军：胡塞恐怖分子使用无人机袭击KAFD大厦
items.summary: RIYADH —The terrorist attack, targeting one of the towers of the King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD) in Riyadh on Tuesday, was carried out by the Houthi milia, using a drone. This was disclosed by Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen. He emphasized that the deliberate targeting of civilians and civilian infrastructure by the terrorist Houthi militia would be met with a firm and decisive response. Eleven people were injured in the terrorist attack, launched by the Houthi militia on Tuesday.

items.title: Culture Ministry introduces insurance consulting service for cultural assets
items.title_zh: 文化部推出文化资产保险咨询服务
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Culture has introduced a cultural insurance consulting service that enables individuals, government entities, and cultural establishments to identify risks to cultural assets and activities and make informed insurance decisions. The service provides specialized advice on insuring artworks, heritage collections, historic buildings, museums, exhibitions, and cultural events. It aims to reduce the financial impact of risks and strengthen the sustainability of cultural assets in the Kingdom. Those wishing to benefit from the service may apply through the ministry's website by selecting the "Inquiry" service on the "Contact Us" page at ‏https://www.moc.gov.sa/Modules/Pages/SocialChannels .

items.title: AI leads tech sector commercial registrations with 31% surge
items.title_zh: 人工智能以31%的增长率领跑科技行业商业登记
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Commerce has reported significant growth in active commercial registrations in promising technology sectors in 2026. This was driven by efforts to facilitate digital transformation and innovation, promote economic diversification, foster entrepreneurship, and support the goals of Saudi Vision 2030. By the end of the third quarter of 2026, active commercial registrations for artificial intelligence technologies rose 31percent to 24,693, compared with 18,846 in the same period of 2025. Registrations in cloud computing services increased 35 percent to 7,362 from 5,466 a year earlier. Active commercial registrations in the cybersecurity sector also grew 22 percent to 11,274 by the end of the third quarter of 2026, from 9,238 in the corresponding period of 2025. Registrations in the electronic gaming industry climbed 25 percent to 981 by the end of the third quarter of 2026, up from 784 in the same period the previous year.

items.title: Al-Jadaan: Non-oil activities record highest contribution to GDP at 57.7%
items.title_zh: 贾达恩：非石油产业对GDP的贡献率创下57.7%的历史新高
items.summary: RIYADH — Minister of Finance Mohammed Al-Jadaan affirmed that the priorities of the state’s general budget for the fiscal year 2027 are centered on continuing to provide essential services to citizens, enhancing their quality of life, directing support to eligible groups, empowering the private sector, stimulating economic growth, and safeguarding the nation’s achievements. He noted that estimated revenues for the coming year stand at SR1.202 trillion, against projected expenditures of SR1.392 trillion, resulting in a deficit of approximately SR190 billion.He made the remarks while addressing the government press conference organized by the Ministry of Media in Riyadh on Tuesday, on the eve of the approval of the state’s general budget for the fiscal year 2027. He outlined the key features of financial and economic performance in 2026, the 2027 budget, public finances over the medium term, the distribution of expenditure across various sectors, and the outlook for economic growth. **media[2799388]**Al-Jadaan explained that the Kingdom has undergone a profound transformation in its economic and development trajectory over the past decade since the launch of Saudi Vision 2030. Non-oil economic activities have expanded, the private sector’s contribution has increased, and the quality of services provided to citizens has improved, despite the successive challenges confronting the global economy.The minister pointed out that Saudi Vision 2030 was launched to restructure the economy and public finances, diversify the economic base and sources of non-oil revenue, empower the private sector, and strengthen the Saudi economy’s capacity to withstand external shocks. “Estimates indicate that the 2026 fiscal year will close with expenditures of approximately SR1.436 trillion and revenues of SR1.191 trillion, resulting in a deficit of SR245 billion, equivalent to around 4.9 percent of GDP. The government had succeeded in maintaining control over deficit levels despite the challenges,” he said.Al-Jadaan stated that although GDP contracted by 2.1 percent due to lower oil production, non-oil GDP continued to register positive growth, accounting for 57.7 percent of total GDP — the highest share in the Kingdom’s history since records began. **media[2799387]**The minister noted that this transformation reflects the growing diversification of the Saudi economy, which is now underpinned by sectors playing an increasingly active role in economic activity, including technology, tourism, industry, and military industries, all of which have recorded substantial growth in recent years. He affirmed that domestic economic indicators demonstrate the economy’s resilience, with domestic demand continuing to expand despite the challenges.Jump in hiring of Saudis in private sector Employment of Saudis in the private sector also rose by 7 percent compared to last year, while the profits of companies listed on the financial market increased by 17 percent through the third quarter compared to the corresponding period last year.The minister noted that the Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) reached 54 points in October, surpassing the average levels recorded by G20 and GCC countries. Meanwhile, the number of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) grew by 4 percent between the end of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, reaching 1.832 million. This growth reflects the promising opportunities that investors and entrepreneurs continue to identify in the Saudi economy.Regarding public finance and banking sector indicators, Al-Jadaan explained that the government maintained its deposits with the Saudi Central Bank at SR399 billion, while the Central Bank’s foreign reserve assets reached SR1.7 trillion by the end of the first half of this year. Bank credit expanded by approximately 7 percent, while non-performing loans remained stable at below 1 percent, placing the Kingdom among the countries with the lowest levels globally. Inflation remained under controlHe noted that inflation remained under control and is expected to reach 1.8 percent this year, despite the International Monetary Fund raising its forecast for global inflation in 2026 from 4.1 percent to 4.7percent, reflecting the effectiveness of the government’s proactive interventions. Al-Jadaan reviewed the performance of non-oil economic activities during the current year, explaining that they recorded growth of 2.8 percent in the first quarter before being affected by the repercussions of the geopolitical crisis and the near-total closure of ports in the eastern region of the Kingdom. Growth resumed in the third quarter following the redirection of import and export traffic to western ports. He expects non-oil GDP to grow by 2.5 percent by the end of this year. **media[2799389]** The minister revealed that the Kingdom had implemented more than 200 interventions since the outbreak of the crisis, covering policies, procedures, regulations, and financing measures. These included facilities extended by national financing funds to borrowers and economic establishments to ensure the availability of sufficient liquidity for working capital and the import of food products, supplies, and production inputs. Al-Jadaan said the royal decree reactivating the SANED program to support sectors affected by the crisis for an initial period of three months aims to preserve the contractual relationship between citizens and employers and prevent its termination as a result of temporary challenges. He also highlighted the formation of a ministerial committee to respond flexibly and swiftly to the needs of business sectors and the exemptions they require.He explained that, for the first time in the Kingdom, the government had established an insurance pool in cooperation with the Insurance Authority and national insurance companies to help reduce insurance costs for shipments arriving at the Kingdom’s ports. This initiative has contributed to lowering insurance costs by approximately 50 percent to 60 percent, with its full impact expected to materialize gradually as new insurance policies are issued. He also highlighted the government’s efforts to facilitate the flow of imports into the Kingdom and other Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries through Red Sea ports by streamlining customs procedures, easing truck entry and exit at ports, simplifying inspection processes, and strengthening coordination mechanisms among countries.Allocation of expendituresRegarding the allocation of expenditure in the 2027 budget, the minister said the education, health, social development, and municipal services sectors would receive approximately SR544 billion. Estimated expenditure on the military sector stands at SR263 billion, representing an increase of approximately SR9 billion compared to the end of the current year.Al-Jadaan explained that the medium-term fiscal projections for 2028 and 2029 are intended to provide the economy and private sector with a clear forward-looking picture of budget priorities and government spending directions. He projected GDP growth of 10 percent in 2027, compared to the 12 percent estimate outlined in the preliminary budget statement. He attributed the revised projection to the increase in oil production during the final three months of this year, which raised the baseline for comparison. He noted that the projected growth would be driven primarily by higher oil production alongside continued expansion in non-oil GDP.The minister indicated that nominal GDP is expected to reach approximately SR5.364 trillion by the end of this year, while inflation is projected to stand at 2.3 percent next year.Al-Jadaan stressed that Saudi Vision 2030 is far more than a project, initiative, or strategy; rather, it represents an ongoing structural transformation encompassing the social, economic, and financial spheres, whose momentum will continue despite challenges. He emphasized that the government’s priorities are to safeguard the nation and its achievements, ensure the provision of essential services to citizens, give the private sector a clear outlook on future policies and government support, and continue developing the vital infrastructure underpinning the economy. Economy demonstrates remarkable resilienceThe minister affirmed that the Saudi economy has demonstrated remarkable resilience and an exceptional ability to withstand economic and geopolitical shocks over the past decades and through successive global crises, consistently emerging stronger and more robust. He noted that the positive results recorded in 2026, together with the realistic projections for 2027, reflect the strength and stability of the Kingdom’s economic foundations.He stated that official figures released by independent entities showed that private sector investments grew at a faster rate through the third quarter of 2026 compared to the previous year, alongside an increase in consumption levels.The minister emphasized that this growth underscores the confidence of local and private investors in the Saudi economy, independently of government expenditure and Public Investment Fund investments. This, he said, makes the budget’s growth targets realistic and achievable. Prudent and disciplined fiscal policy Al-Jadaan clarified that the government’s fiscal policy follows a prudent and disciplined approach to preparing annual budget estimates, relying on realistic assumptions while avoiding exaggeration and excessive optimism. This approach has resulted in actual revenues exceeding budget estimates in recent years. The minister pointed out that rising sovereign debt levels are among the most significant risks confronting the global economy today. The issue featured prominently in discussions at the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, particularly as debt in some countries has exceeded 100 percent of GDP.He affirmed that the Kingdom enjoys a strong financial position, with debt levels remaining safe and sound relative to GDP. He explained that debt-servicing costs as a proportion of total revenues remain within acceptable limits, while the economic returns generated by borrowing more than offset its costs.Al-Jadaan reassured the public about the impact of rising global interest rates on the Kingdom’s public debt portfolio, explaining that between 89 percent and 90 percent of government debt carries fixed rather than variable interest rates. He noted that more than half of the portfolio was borrowed at interest rates below 3 percent. He stressed that there was no cause for concern over the medium term, crediting the efficient management of the National Debt Management Center and its team of highly qualified young Saudi professionals, who oversee the portfolio with exceptional expertise.National Privatization StrategyRegarding the transition from the National Privatization Program to the National Privatization Strategy, the minister explained that the program had laid the necessary foundations and culminated in the development of the ambitious National Privatization Strategy. He noted that approximately 200 privatization contracts had been signed since 2017, with a combined value estimated at around SR800 billion. These contracts covered asset sales and public-private partnerships, helping to empower the private sector and enhance the efficiency of government projects during both the construction and operational phases.Al-Jadaan affirmed that privatization efforts are continuing, revealing that approximately 202 projects are currently at various stages of tendering, bid submission, and evaluation. These projects span several sectors, including water, electricity, health, environment, transportation, and real estate, in addition to a number of other sectors.

items.title: 11 injured in Houthi attack on Riyadh’s financial district tower
items.title_zh: 胡塞武装袭击利雅得金融区大楼，造成11人受伤
items.summary: RIYADH — Eleven people were injured in a terrorist attack, launched by the Houthi militia on Tuesday, targeting one of the towers of the financial district in Riyadh. The injured people included two Saudi citizens, four Egyptian residents, three Nepalese residents, and two Indian residents, according to the spokesperson of the Civil Defense.The spokesperson stated that the relevant authorities responded swiftly to the incident, implementing all approved emergency procedures and measures and taking every necessary step to safeguard lives and property.Earlier on the day, Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen, revealed that one of the towers of the financial district in Riyadh had been targeted in a cowardly terrorist attack.

items.title: Crown Prince: 2027 budget transforms Vision 2030 achievements into lasting economic strength
items.title_zh: 王储：2027年预算将“2030愿景”的成就转化为持久的经济实力
items.summary: RIYADH — Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman underscored that the 2027 budget reflects the government's unwavering commitment to advancing national development, placing citizens' interests at the heart of its priorities, and safeguarding the Kingdom's development achievements to ensure their sustainability for generations to come. In post budgetary remarks after approval of the state’s general budget for the fiscal year 2027 by the Cabinet, the Crown Prince, who is also chairman of the Council of Economic and Development Affairs, noted that the achievements realized so far are the result of the directives of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and the efforts of citizens. The Crown Prince stated that work in the third phase of Saudi Vision 2030 builds upon the reforms and accomplishments achieved during the previous two phases. "We are maximizing the impact of the Vision on people's lives, transforming its achievements into a sustainable strength for our economy and renewed opportunities for future generations,” he said. The Crown Prince emphasized the continued expansion of development opportunities, investment in the capabilities of Saudi citizens, and the building of a more diverse and competitive economy whose impact extends beyond 2030. The Crown Prince affirmed that the 2027 budget is part of a long-term financial plan that balances supporting sustainable growth, implementing development priorities, and strengthening public finance sustainability, while maintaining flexibility in resource allocation and continued funding for programs and projects with economic and social impact. He noted that enhancing the effectiveness of the social support and protection system—by directing spending to those most in need and raising living standards and quality of life—remains a core priority within Saudi Arabia's fiscal and economic policy, alongside continued investment in infrastructure and essential services for citizens, residents, and visitors, and the development of transport and logistics networks to strengthen regional connectivity, enhance investment appeal, improve the efficiency of goods movement, and bolster economic resilience against shifts in global supply chains. The Crown Prince underscored the importance of increasing spending efficiency, measuring its outcomes, aligning resource allocation with national strategies, and maximizing returns from government assets and investments. He stressed that government entities are responsible for ensuring high-quality monitoring, execution, and transparency, as well as achieving targeted project outcomes that support medium- and long-term development. He further noted that economic reforms and policies supporting economic activity have broadened the economic base and enhanced competitiveness, pointing out that 2026 estimates indicate a 2.5 percent growth in real GDP from non-oil activities, reflecting progress in economic diversification plans. The Crown Prince stated that financial sector growth, underpinned by strong regulatory frameworks, supports economic financing and private sector expansion, and that maintaining the strength of Saudi Arabia's financial position facilitates access to financial markets and diversifies funding sources while keeping public debt at sustainable levels and maintaining substantial government reserves to navigate changes and sustain development. He commended the private sector's role in driving economic growth amid ongoing regulatory and structural reforms aimed at developing the business environment, enhancing investment stability and attractiveness for local and international investors, expanding investment opportunities, increasing the private sector's economic contribution, and supporting small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), local content development, non-oil exports, and job creation. The Crown Prince affirmed that the Public Investment Fund (PIF) continues to develop strategic and promising sectors aligned with development priorities and economic diversification by strengthening partnerships with the private sector and supporting SMEs through investments that localize knowledge, develop national talent, enhance local content in the fund's operations, and expand investment opportunities in domestic and global markets. Complementing this role, the Crown Prince said that the National Development Fund, through its affiliated development funds and banks, continues to enhance financing efficiency, direct funding toward national priorities, expand financing opportunities for development sectors and projects, and incentivize private sector participation to support the budget and maximize the developmental impact of available resources. Internationally, the Crown Prince stressed that Saudi Arabia has demonstrated its capability and standing as a sustainable and reliable global supplier in securing world energy supplies, backed by strategic investments in energy and logistics infrastructure to ensure the flow of oil and non-oil exports by utilizing the East-West Pipeline and ports along the western coast. He reaffirmed the Kingdom's commitment to continued cooperation with producing countries, expanding economic partnerships, and contributing to efforts supporting regional and global development and stability, in line with Saudi Arabia's international standing and responsibility. The Crown Prince stated that current geopolitical developments have demonstrated the resilience of the Saudi economy and its high capacity to adapt to changing circumstances through flexible fiscal policies and effective coordination among entities. He noted that the Kingdom closely monitors all regional and global developments, including uncertainty in the global economy, stressing that national security and stability are the foundation for preserving development achievements and continuing to develop military and defense capabilities. He expressed his pride in the officers and personnel of the armed forces and security sectors, including those stationed along the nation's borders, for their efforts and sacrifices in defending the Kingdom and its assets. The Crown Prince also affirmed that Saudi Arabia, under the leadership and directives of King Salman, continues to expand opportunities for its citizens, safeguard its stability, security, and inviolable sovereignty, and defend its assets with strength and determination. “The Kingdom pursues comprehensive growth and development across all sectors and reinforces its active role in the global economy and establishes the foundations of peace and stability in the region and the world with wisdom and objectivity,” he added.
